Three inconsistent\nregimes existed across a 12-asset panel:\n\n| Regime | Assets | `cycle_source` | C4 bottom populated? |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| guarded (correct) | BTC only | \u2014 | no |\n| empty bottom | gold, ndx, riot, spx, wgmi | `actual_C4_open` | no |\n| **populated bottom** | eth, xrp, sol, mstr, mara, dxy, tlt | `actual` | **yes** |\n\n`D_asset_top_to_next_bottom` / `drawdown_asset_pct` therefore reported\n`n_actual=4` for dxy and tlt but `n_actual=3` for gold/ndx/spx on the **same\nstatistic**, and the 7 contaminated values entered the quantile fits.\n\n## Root cause\n\n`scripts/build_alt_cycle_metrics.py:301-304` (original):\n\n```python\nif cid == \"C4\" and cycle_source == \"actual\":\n    if row_data.get(\"asset_next_bear_bottom_date\") == \"\":\n        cycle_source = \"actual_C4_open\"\n```\n\nThe open-cycle marker keyed off whether the bottom happened to be **empty**,\nnot off whether the **cycle** was open. So any open cycle whose running minimum\nhad already been found kept `cycle_source=\"actual\"` \u2014 asserting a final bottom\nfor a cycle whose next halving (H5) is still 1.5 years away.\n\nTwo independent guards existed in the codebase, and disagreed:\n- `build_cycle_metrics.py:203-211` (BTC) correctly skips Rule B when the\n  canonical bottom is `not_yet_observed`.\n- `build_alt_next_cycle_zones.py:506,516-517` hardcoded `if cid == \"C4\": post = None`.\n- `_extract_multiplier_series` / `_extract_drawdown_series` and\n  `build_alt_forward_ranges.py:41` (`ACTUAL_SOURCES = {\"actual\", \"actual_C4_open\"}`)\n  had no notion of an unconfirmed bottom at all.\n\n**Why refreshing data could never fix this.** Rule B's window for C4 runs to\n`H5 - 30d = 2028-03-02`, far beyond the available data (2026-09-21). The C4\n\"bottom\" is therefore a **running minimum with no right edge**: it can only\nfall, never rise. Proof it was already an artifact rather than an event \u2014\n`tlt`'s C4 bottom was `2026-08-14`, exactly its `asset_last_data_date`\n(gap 0 days), i.e. the last row of the file. BTC gained the same fields for parity.\n2. **Fixed the label** to key off cycle openness\n   (`cycle_closed = next_halving <= data_cutoff`).\n3. **Per-statistic eligibility** in `build_alt_forward_ranges.py`. Eligibility is\n   a property of the statistic, not the asset:\n   - bottom-dependent (`D_asset_top_to_next_bottom`, `drawdown_asset_pct`) require\n     a closed cycle;\n   - top-dependent (`mult_asset_bottom_to_top`, `D_asset_*_halving_to_top`,\n     `D_asset_prev_bottom_to_halving`) legitimately include the open cycle \u2014\n     `mult = top / pre_halving_bottom` needs only two observed quantities.\n   Enforced structurally, not by relying on the value being empty.\n4. **Replaced the hardcoded `cid == \"C4\"`** in `build_alt_next_cycle_zones.py`\n   with a `bottom_status` check so it generalises to C5.\n5. **Surfaced it.** `bottom_tracking` in `_data/cycle_status.json` for BTC and\n   every asset block, rendered in the `now-stamp` banner (interactive row +\n   `noscript` fallback), always labelled *provisional*.\n\n## Three further defects found by the new gates\n\nThese were not the reported symptom but were caught by\n`tests/test_bottom_status.py` while verifying the fix.\n\n1. **Rule T/B could emit an extremum outside its own window.** The \u00b121d\n   neighbourhood re-pick is unguarded, so WGMI produced a C4 \"bottom\" at\n   `2026-09-01`, only **75 days** after its top \u2014 before Rule B's own\n   `top+90d` window start. Fixed by clamping the date to `[window_start,\n   window_end]` and re-reading the price **at the clamped date** (clamping the\n   date alone left a date spliced onto a foreign price: WGMI returned\n   `$41.28` @ 2026-09-16 against a true window low of `$44.56`).\n   Verified a no-op for BTC C1\u2013C3 (tops, bottoms and all D-values identical).\n2. **Non-deterministic multi-source merge.** `build_alt_cycle_metrics.py:97` and\n   `build_curve_state.py:82` did `sort_values(\"date\")` \u2014 pandas' default\n   **unstable** quicksort \u2014 *before* `drop_duplicates(keep=\"last\")`. The\n   \"later source wins\" tie-break on a shared date was therefore arbitrary\n   between runs; observed as gold's C4 provisional low differing by `$6.50`\n   from a recomputation of the same window. Fixed with `kind=\"stable\"`.\n3. **`n_with_proxy` under-counted WGMI.** `PROXY_SOURCES` hardcoded only\n   `ETH_proxy_C1/C2`, so WGMI's `mara_proxy_*` rows fed the statistics while\n   being counted in neither `n_actual` nor `n_with_proxy`. Replaced with a\n   `\"proxy\" in src` predicate.\n\n## Expected vs actual\n\n| Quantity | Before | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| C4 `bottom_status` states | 3 regimes | 1 (`provisional_low_to_date` / `none`) |\n| `n_actual` (dxy, tlt) on `D_asset_top_to_next_bottom` | 4 | 3 |\n| `n_actual` (gold, ndx, spx) on `mult_asset_bottom_to_top` | 4 | 4 (unchanged \u2014 legitimate) |\n| BTC C1\u2013C3 metrics | \u2014 | byte-identical |\n| Pipeline idempotence | 0 processed CSVs changed over 2 runs | 0 (re-verified) |\n\n## Verification\n\n`tests/test_bottom_status.py` \u2014 13 new gates, including an independent\nrecomputation of the running minimum from the raw snapshots (not a\nself-consistency check), which is what caught defects 1 and 2 above.\nSuite: **224 passed**. Chart PNG snapshots re-pinned once after the numeric\nchange; Jekyll build clean.\n\n## Follow-ups deliberately NOT taken\n\n- **Open-cycle TOPS have the same defect and were left alone.** Rule T's window\n  for C4 runs to `H5 - 270d`, so the C4 top is also a running maximum. SPX's is\n  `2026-08-13` with data ending `2026-08-14` \u2014 one day of confirmation. This is\n  the same class of problem applied to tops and needs its own increment.\n- **Zone-band overlap** (audit finding #1) is *not* fixed here. Removing the\n  provisional observations changes the exit-zone quantiles that produced it, so\n  it must be re-measured against the new statistics rather than clamped blindly.\n- **Dual bottom price** (events.csv intraday vs Rule B close, up to +1.84%)\n  remains open \u2014 that is a source-of-truth ruling, not a computation.\n",

```python
# R-5: the four zones are mutually non-overlapping. exit_base_start is
# computed independently as H5 + median(D_halving_to_top) + q25(D_top_to_next_bottom),
# which collides with the distribution window whenever
# median(ht) + q25(tnb) < q75(ht) -- true for every asset whose top-window
# IQR exceeds its lower-quartile post-top-to-bottom duration (gold: IQR 549d
# vs q25 119d). Shift the exit band forward, preserving its width, so it
# starts the day after the distribution band closes.
def _shift_after(band_start, band_end, floor_date):
    delta = (floor_date - band_start).days
    if delta > 0:
        return floor_date, band_end + timedelta(days=delta)
    return band_start, band_end

    exit_outer_start, exit_outer_end, dist_outer_end + timedelta(days=1))
```

- On Linux CI → LF bytes → different SHA → mismatch.

So the manifest SHAs are line-ending dependent. Structurally guaranteed to fail on CI.

This is EXACTLY what `docs/github-workflow.md` §7 warned about, and the prescribed fix there was to normalize and regenerate hashes from the LF blobs — which was apparently never completed (or was undone by subsequent Windows fetches writing new manifests with CRLF SHAs).

Now: what's the right fix? Two clean options:

**Option A — make the manifest hash line-ending-independent.** Compute SHA over bytes with `\r\n` normalized to `\n`. Both Windows and Linux then agree. Requires changing `_sha256_file` in every fetch script (fetch_macro, fetch_alts, fetch_data, fetch_yields) AND the test helpers, AND regenerating the manifest. **Option B — stop normalizing CSVs.** Add `*.csv -text` (or remove the csv line) to `.gitattributes` so git stores bytes verbatim. Option B is minimal and immediately makes the existing manifest valid on both platforms. The last failure had two causes, both pre-existing design issues rather than anything from the audit:

```python
def _load_pipeline_module():
    import importlib.util
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("refresh_all", SCRIPT)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


def test_corr_phase_precedes_regime_robustness():
    """build_regime_robustness reads correlations_phase.csv, so build_correlations_phase
    must run to completion first — never concurrently in the same parallel stage."""
    mod = _load_pipeline_module()
    stages = mod.build_pipeline(skip_fetch=False)

    def locate(step_name):
        for si, st in enumerate(stages):
            for step in st.steps:
                if step.name == step_name:
                    return si, st
        return None, None

    corr_si, corr_stage = locate("corr_phase")
    reg_si, reg_stage = locate("regime")
    assert corr_si is not None, "corr_phase step missing from pipeline"
    assert reg_si is not None, "regime step missing from pipeline"
    # Must not share a parallel stage (that is the race).
    assert corr_si != reg_si, (
        "corr_phase and regime are in the same stage; regime reads "
        "correlations_phase.csv, so they must be serialized"
    )
    # And corr_phase must come strictly earlier.
    assert corr_si < reg_si, "corr_phase must run before regime robustness"
```

```python
"""Atomic writes for pipeline artefacts (data/processed CSVs, JSON, includes, Pine).

Every artefact is written to a sibling temp file and moved into place with
os.replace(), so:

* readers never observe a partially-written file (the corr_phase -> regime
  read/write race class of bug),
* a failed or interrupted write never truncates the previous good output,
* writes survive transient open(..., "w") failures observed on external
  drives, where in-place truncating opens of existing files intermittently
  fail with EINVAL while fresh file creation and rename-over keep working.

The temp file is removed on failure; a successful call leaves no residue.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path


def atomic_to_csv(df, path, **to_csv_kwargs):
    """df.to_csv(path, **kwargs), atomically (write tmp + os.replace)."""
    dest = Path(path)
    tmp = dest.with_name(dest.name + ".tmp")
    try:
        df.to_csv(tmp, **to_csv_kwargs)
        os.replace(tmp, dest)
    except BaseException:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise


def atomic_write_text(path, text, encoding="utf-8", newline=""):
    """Write text to path atomically (mirrors Path.write_text + newline arg)."""
    dest = Path(path)
    tmp = dest.with_name(dest.name + ".tmp")
    try:
        with open(tmp, "w", encoding=encoding, newline=newline) as f:
            f.write(text)
        os.replace(tmp, dest)
    except BaseException:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise


def atomic_write_json(path, data, encoding="utf-8", **json_kwargs):
    """json.dump(data, f) to path atomically."""
    dest = Path(path)
    tmp = dest.with_name(dest.name + ".tmp")
    try:
        with open(tmp, "w", encoding=encoding, newline="") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, **json_kwargs)
        os.replace(tmp, dest)
    except BaseException:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
```

Test design:

```python
"""Atomic-write helpers (scripts/csv_io.py): unit gates + convention scan.

The pipeline must write every derived artefact via csv_io.atomic_* so that
(a) readers never see partial files (corr_phase -> regime race class),
(b) a failed write never truncates the previous good output,
(c) writes survive transient open(...,'w') EINVAL failures observed on
    external drives (in-place truncate fails; fresh-file + rename works).
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))

from csv_io import atomic_to_csv, atomic_write_json, atomic_write_text


def test_atomic_to_csv_roundtrip(tmp_path):
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": ["x", "y"]})
    dest = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    atomic_to_csv(df, dest, index=False)
    assert dest.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == df.to_csv(index=False)  # byte-identical
    assert not list(tmp_path.glob("*.tmp"))


def test_atomic_write_text_platform_newline(tmp_path):
    dest = tmp_path / "out.txt"
    atomic_write_text(dest, "a\nb\n", encoding="utf-8")
    plain = tmp_path / "plain.txt"
    plain.write_text("a\nb\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert dest.read_bytes() == plain.read_bytes()  # newline translation identical
    assert not list(tmp_path.glob("*.tmp"))


def test_atomic_write_json_roundtrip(tmp_path):
    dest = tmp_path / "out.json"
    atomic_write_json(dest, {"b": 1, "a": [2]}, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    assert json.loads(dest.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == {"a": [2], "b": 1}
    assert not list(tmp_path.glob("*.tmp"))


def test_atomic_failure_cleans_tmp_and_keeps_previous(tmp_path):
    dest = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    dest.write_text("previous", encoding="utf-8")
    class Boom(pd.DataFrame):  # to_csv that raises mid-write
        def to_csv(self, *a, **k):
            raise RuntimeError("boom")
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        atomic_to_csv(Boom(), dest)
    assert dest.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "previous"  # not truncated
    assert not list(tmp_path.glob("*.tmp"))


PIPELINE_SCRIPTS = [...]

def test_pipeline_scripts_have_no_raw_artifact_writes():
    ... scan ...
```
